A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NodeDup research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original link-prediction experiments, baseline comparisons, runtime measurements and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator experiments and diagnostic analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: NodeDup retains the same four-step duplication, edge augmentation and supervised training procedure. NodeDup(L) still adds self-loops for aggregation and supervision. Algorithm 1 is relocated, while the additional encoder experiments apply the existing augmentation without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Chameleon and Squirrel heterophilic graphs and a MovieLens-1M movie recommendation task constructed from shared positive ratings (Appendices C.4–C.5). These extend the represented graph conditions and application domain. The original seven benchmarks, inductive scenarios and IGB-1M evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds GRADE and SAILOR comparisons on Cora and Citeseer using GCN (Table 13), plus GCN and GraphTransformer controls (Table 17). The existing principal baseline sets remain. NodeDup(L) is omitted from the consolidated upsampling comparison in Table 12, although its corresponding benchmark scores remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: v2 removes the complete MRR evaluation reported in v1 Appendix D.2 and introduces AUC evaluation separately for Warm-Warm and Warm-Cold links (Table 5). It also adds matched-GCN comparator experiments, GraphTransformer settings and MovieLens graph construction. The retained benchmarks keep their original splits, 500 negative candidates, Hits@10 protocol and stated training settings.

E4.justification: New analyses examine the source of warm-node gains through link-type stratification, extend the node-type ablation to NodeDup(L) and computation/memory costs, and investigate GCN/GraphTransformer dependence. Figure 11 adds efficiency comparisons against cold-start baselines. The duplication-frequency heatmaps and SEAL experiments already existed in v1 and are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both implementation sections specify results over 10 random seeds, and matched result tables retain the same plus/minus reporting. v2 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical estimation procedures. Additional result rows do not establish additional runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Matched main Tables 1–4 and retained appendix results are unchanged. v2 adds heterophily, MovieLens, GRADE/SAILOR, GCN/GraphTransformer, resource and stratified-link results. For example, new Table 5 reports Citeseer Warm-Cold AUC of 88.40±0.92 for NodeDup and 85.40±0.78 for GSage. The full MRR results in v1 Table 7 are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the additional decoder complexity from O((M + |V_cold|)D) in v1 to O(|V_cold|D) in v2. The final overall complexity expression, message-passing mathematics and self-distillation derivation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of inexpensive, plug-and-play cold-start improvement while preserving warm-node performance. The headline improvements of 38.49%, 13.34% and 6.76% remain. Calling these improvements relative and replacing 'state-of-the-art' with 'existing' methods does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 attributes warm-node gains primarily to improved cold endpoints (Sections 4.2 and 4.8), explains smaller GCN gains through supervision without separate aggregation views, and proposes explanations for GRADE/SAILOR weaknesses. Appendix E adds a substantive limitation concerning connected nodes with dissimilar features, beyond v1's warning about generalization to node classification.

D1.justification: The documented implementation location changes from snap-research/NodeDup to zhichunguo/NodeDup. v2 also describes MovieLens graph construction, explicitly states equal node counts for random and cold-node duplication, and adds resource measurements. The disclosed model dimensions, dropout, learning-rate searches, software and GPU remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of incremental recommendation learning and adds references supporting GRADE, SAILOR, GraphTransformer and the new datasets/task. It removes the molecular-representation review cited as Guo et al. (2022a). The principal positioning as an augmentation requiring no architectural modification remains intact.

P1.justification: Much of the prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 revises mechanism explanations, moves Algorithm 1 and the duplication-frequency discussion into the main text, rearranges appendix experiments and adds appendix navigation. Front matter and acknowledgements change, while the existing impact statement becomes an Ethics Statement appendix.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout. v2 adds aggregation/supervision diagrams (Figures 2, 3 and 7), a cold-start runtime figure and new result tables. It expands the node-type table with NodeDup(L) and resource columns, merges heuristic/upsampling displays, removes the MRR table and relocates existing figures.

improvement.justification: The warm-link breakdown, broader evaluations and resource ablations improve support for applicability and efficiency, while the expanded limitations clarify where generalization remains untested. These benefits outweigh the removal of MRR evidence. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Appendix C.2 misquotes Table 8 values, and C.4 claims improvement in every setting despite small NodeDup declines on Chameleon in Table 10.
